condensation.recordedBy: the P1 condensation fix session, from the presenter's letter in the session prompt
condensation.ruling: THE CONDENSATION LANDS ON A SMOOTH LUMINOUS BALL THAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT THE MARK. Pure-white monochrome per P1's register — no warm tone, no orange anywhere near it — with a tighter, cooler glow falloff than the ClaimMark's, sized per the reopened cell's box. It must read as premium and intentional as a still and stay clearly distinct from the Claim Mark at a glance.
condensation.reopened: p1-b3 — the granular condensed mass is presenter-reopened and superseded by p1-b3-ball. The retired cell stays on file (aesthetic-law file-keeping clause).
condensation.scope: The condensation landing only. Audited rather than assumed: P1's _applyBuild puts the condensed object on stage at exactly one build (setVisible(mass, n === 3)) and nowhere else, so no adjacent state shows the condensed mass before the shell. No other P1 cell is affected, and the letter changes no other beat.
condensation.notAmended: Letter B leaves the master's no-anticipation rule untouched: the ball is not the mark, so the birth in Scene 3 stays the accent's first appearance and the disc's first appearance. The freeze-register amendment the brief reserves for letter A is NOT made.
condensation.superseded: SUPERSEDED 30 August 2026 by rulings.restoration — the condensation is PORT, and p1-b3-ball retires beside p1-b3. Kept in full: it is the record of what was ruled, and the restoration's trail needs it.

restoration.recordedBy: the P1 restoration session, from the presenter's ruling in the session prompt
restoration.ruling: P1'S CONDENSATION IS PORT. The legacy deck's absorption is the proven treatment and is restored VERBATIM: the field's points absorbed gradually into the luminous white ball, using the legacy slides' own gesture — the legacy implementation ported (timing, easing, absorption behavior, the ball's rendering), not re-authored from description. The ball is the legacy ball, verbatim. The test is that it looks exactly as it always did.
restoration.legacySource: 1-02-the-conversion (src/slides/section-1-question/02-the-conversion.js) — COLLAPSE_MS 4600, TOKEN_EMERGE_AT 0.22, and the object it renders: `.luminous-disc` + `.s1q-token` (src/styles/slides.css), 176px centred on the stage at (960, 540), arriving from scale(0.82) over 1100ms opacity / 1500ms transform.
restoration.reopened: BOTH prior candidates. p1-b3 (the granular mass, 29 Aug) and p1-b3-ball (the white monochrome ball, 30 Aug) are superseded-by-restoration and stay on file under the aesthetic law's file-keeping clause.

strickenClause.verdict: STRUCK as over-extension — it was that document's own invention, not the architecture's law. Struck in place at its origin, with a pointer to the trail.
strickenClause.replacedBy: orange enters the film at Scene 3's birth; no accent color in the Prologue — docs/what-is-money-master.md §8.5 and its freeze register, 25 August 2026. Unchanged, and always the law.
strickenClause.cost: The clause is what made P1's condensation a design question at all: it ruled out the one object the deck had already proven for this gesture, and the beat went to the candidate process instead — a granular mass, a reopening, a white ball, a second reopening, two retired cells, for a frame that was never open.

restoration.notAmended: The freeze register, the master and the architecture are untouched. Under PORT the condensation lands on the deck's proven token, which is the same drawing as the Claim Mark's disc — so the no-anticipation question the letter-A branch would have raised returns. It is FLAGGED for the presenter, not decided here (docs/p1-restoration-and-provenance-report.md §7).
